transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-24
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Cam Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Aisha Patel (Cascade Care - Head of ML), Marc Ruiz (CTO), Lina Gomez (DevOps), Daniel Cho (Product), Samir Khan (Security)

Summary:
Quick onboarding/kickoff for Cascade Care to get Redwood set up for a 2-week pilot focused on chat assistant and embeddings for triage. Discussed hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), SSO and compliance needs, initial success criteria, and next steps to set up sandbox and benchmarks.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and success criteria
- Network and VPC connectivity options
- Security: SOC2, KMS, data retention
- Model selection and perf expectations
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we've got Priya (our SE) and Cam our CSM, and from Cascade Care we've got Aisha, Marc, Lina, Daniel, and Samir. thanks for taking the time.

[00:18] Aisha Patel: Hey thanks Jordan, excited to get started. we carved out time for a 2 week pilot to see latency/cost on our triage flows.

[00:28] Marc Ruiz: Yeah main things for us are latency under 400 ms for single-turn generation, cost roughly in line with our forecast, and security - we need to validate we can meet our HIPAA-ish controls and SOC2 requests.

[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Awesome. quick overview from the technical side: Redwood offers hosted API which is fastest to get going, Dedicated reserved pools if you need predictable throughput, and Private mode for VPC/on-prem. For pilot i'd recommend hosted or dedicated with VPC peering depending on your network constraints.

[01:10] Lina Gomez: Quick Q, is VPC peering available for hosted? like can we keep traffic inside our VPC?

[01:18] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have a Private deployment option that supports customer-managed VPC peering and private control plane; for hosted we do have regional endpoints but if you require direct peering we'd look at Private or Dedicated with VPC peering. small note: peering setup times vary by cloud.

[01:40] Samir Khan: On encryption - do you support customer-managed keys? we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.

[01:47] Cam Nguyen: Yes, we support KMS integrations for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured to use CMK per contract. we also have audit logging and trace hooks in the console; i'll share the SOC2 and security pack after the call.

[02:05] Daniel Cho: For the pilot success criteria, Aisha put together a doc - reduce false triage by 15%, latency sub 400ms, and cost per 1K tokens below $X. we'll share exact numbers.

[02:20] Aisha Patel: Correct. also want to test embeddings for semantic search, so we'll need an embeddings endpoint and some batch ingestion.

[02:28] Priya Kapoor: Great, embeddings are supported via our embeddings API; we can recommend quantized model variants for lower cost, and we have batching/caching knobs that help with ingestion. for the pilot we'll preset some recommended config.

[02:45] Marc Ruiz: On model selection — do you curate models, and can we pin a specific model / rollback?

[02:53] Jordan Lee: Yes, the model catalog has verified performance profiles; you can pin model versions and we support rollout controls for canary/rollback. for pilot we typically pick a stable open model we trust and test one quantized and one fp16 variant.

[03:15] Marc Ruiz: Any competitors we should know — marketplace comparisons?

[03:20] Jordan Lee: Customers sometimes compare to Anthropic, OpenAI, and deploying on SageMaker — we can share a short benchmark spreadsheet showing latency vs cost tradeoffs.

[03:30] Lina Gomez: About networking — what information do you need from our side to get VPC peering or Private set up?

[03:36] Priya Kapoor: We'll need your network diagram, CIDR blocks, any egress rules, and the list of subnets/nat gateways. For hosted quickstart we can do API keys over HTTPS, but for Private we'll coordinate peering and routing.

[03:58] Samir Khan: Also SSO — we need SAML or OIDC for RBAC and SCIM for provisioning.

[04:05] Cam Nguyen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC roles; i'll include the SSO guide.

[04:15] Aisha Patel: timeline question — how long to get a sandbox going where we can run perf benchmarks?

[04:22] Priya Kapoor: If hosted only, we can give keys and endpoints same day; for Dedicated or Private with peering, typical lead time is 1-2 weeks depending on approvals and network setup. for pilot i'd aim for hosted sandbox immediately and we can do Dedicated if you want predictable throughput.

[04:45] Marc Ruiz: We prefer to try hosted sandbox first then upgrade to Dedicated if throughput/latency issues show up. success criteria will inform that.

[05:00] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. For the perf plan we'll run generation latency tests (single-turn, 32 tokens), long-context streaming tests, and embeddings throughput for batch sizes of 64/128. we'll capture token-level cost.

[05:20] Daniel Cho: Can you run an initial benchmark on our sample dataset or do we need to push data to your sandbox?

[05:28] Priya Kapoor: We'll need access to sample payloads; for embeddings ingestion you can push to the sandbox or we can arrange a secure transfer. Also, a note: we do prefix/KV caching which can affect latency results, so we'll turn caching off for baseline runs.

[05:50] Aisha Patel: Are there limits on retention or data residency? we have some regional constraints for patient data.

[05:58] Cam Nguyen: We have configurable retention policies and private deployment for strict residency; for hosted we can request region-specific endpoints but Private is best for strict residency. i'll attach the data retention options doc.

[06:15] Marc Ruiz: About pricing — what's the pilot cost and how does billing work for hosted vs Dedicated?

[06:23] Jordan Lee: For pilot we usually provide credits and usage-based billing for hosted; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract monthly. i'll send a pricing sheet with example unit economics for generation and embeddings.

[06:40] Samir Khan: Do you have a formal security questionnaire or ATO paperwork we can start with?

[06:46] Cam Nguyen: Yes, we have an SRA and SOC2 package; i'll share our security questionnaire and contact for compliance.

[07:00] Priya Kapoor: small tech detail — what are your typical sequence lengths and concurrency for triage? this affects kernel selection and batching.

[07:08] Aisha Patel: Typical single message ~ 40-80 tokens, sometimes longer threads up to 1,000 tokens; concurrency for triage can spike to ~120 qps during morning ramp.

[07:22] Priya Kapoor: Good to know — for 1,000 token tails we may recommend a model variant optimized for long context and dynamic kv cache; batching policy will also be tuned to keep tail latency under SLOs.

[07:40] Marc Ruiz: Are there any rate limits we should be aware of during the pilot?

[07:45] Jordan Lee: We'll set quotas for the pilot and you can request bursts; dedicated pools give you higher guaranteed throughput.

[07:55] Lina Gomez: Do you provide client SDKs? we prefer a node/python SDK and maybe a k8s operator.

[08:02] Priya Kapoor: Yes, SDKs for Node/Python and a deployment operator for k8s are available. i'll link to the SDK repo and quickstart.

[08:15] Daniel Cho: On rolling updates — if you pin a model and you want to roll later, how do rollouts work?

[08:22] Jordan Lee: We support canary rollouts and A/B tests at the route level; you can rollback to a pinned version pretty quickly. we'll outline the rollback policy.

[08:35] Aisha Patel: OK can we walk through immediate next steps?

[08:38] Cam Nguyen: Sure: 1) Jordan sends onboarding deck and pricing spreadsheet, 2) Cam shares SSO and SOC2 pack, 3) Priya will create sandbox and start perf plan, 4) Lina shares network diagram and Samir shares KMS requirements.

[08:58] Marc Ruiz: We'll get those items back to you within a week, aiming to start the pilot the week of Aug 3rd.

[09:06] Priya Kapoor: Great. i'll also set up a follow-up technical deep-dive to run through the runbook and perf checklist. suggested time next Tuesday.

[09:15] Aisha Patel: Tuesday works. thanks everyone.

[09:20] Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials.

[09:25] (end)
